entries.final_answer: (1) Zip: the extractor walks the central directory itself from the EOCD (and ZIP64) record before opening ZipFile; it stops and refuses (too_many_entries) past 10,000 headers, refuses a count that does not match the headers found (zip_count_mismatch), and refuses a header whose extra-field length exceeds 1,024 bytes (zip_extra_field_too_large); ZipFile is opened only after the walk passes. (2) Tar: a PAX extended (x), PAX global (g) or GNU long-name/long-link (L/K) header larger than 64 KiB is refused (header_too_large) before the library parses it. (3) A PAX or GNU long name that begins with / is refused as path_absolute (the spec refuses absolute paths), not made relative. (4) A runtime exception from commons-compress becomes a 422 archive_unreadable refusal, never a 500.

entries.final_answer: Amends DM-01M6V4WMF8CD8NBN7A065E9ZQ5. The salvage reads every file on its own, as plain YAML, so one bad file never costs another file's facts. (2) Artifact ids: an artifact file that fails the schema counts by its id: key read as plain YAML, and by the id its path names only when that key cannot be read; when the two differ, both ids count as removed-or-kept candidates (gate and scan both). It uses #416's invalidation rule, the per-pack PackWriteGeneration keyed by the configured name (#418 R5), plus the pack revision (content digest) so an out-of-band edit misses (#416 invariant 4). It never fills from a read whose generation was odd or moved, nor from a RegistryWriteLock holder's staged session (inv. 2, 3). Failures are not cached (inv. 6). Entries are capped with a test above the cap (inv. 5). It stays in packs.application with no storage types, and HexagonalArchitectureTest stays unchanged (inv. 8). The PackWriteGeneration javadoc about 'the facts cache' becomes true. #416 may later fold it into option A/B.

entries.rationale: Runner, 2026-11-08, from the WP24 review (F2, F3). #408 ruling 3 lists an artifact reached only through suggests as a suggestion: something the client may still choose.
